submission.natural_language_explanation: N53+ fires on a token that is a piece of a larger word-like composite rather than a word in its own right: subword/compound continuation fragments that attach to the preceding token with no space ('up' in signup, 'editor' in equationeditor, 'Value' in sameValue, 'net' in testnet, 'AA' in NEAA, 'cho' in ancho, 'ver' in Sil've'ru, a replacement char in a mojibake run) and the seam punctuation inside identifiers, tags and expressions ('->', '.', '_', '^', '>', '":'). Within one word activity jumps sharply at the non-initial piece (' sign' 1.1 vs 'up' 3.8; ' (NE' 1.9 vs 'AA' 3.8; ' same' 2.3 vs 'Value' 3.8), independent space-initial words are weak, and the firing rate rises with bracket/indent nesting (bracket depth 0: 49% vs 8+: 80%), so the feature is 'I am inside an unfinished composite unit', not any particular token or word.

rival_explanations: The pole is an in-context copy/induction detector rather than a surface-composite detector: it peaks only where a chunk already emitted earlier in the same context (a repeated identifier, a repeated closing tag, a repeated list item) is being reproduced, so it should fall sharply when the earlier occurrence is removed even though the peaking piece is unchanged.

The pole is a code-structure/nesting feature that fires on any token sitting deep inside nested brackets or indentation, whatever its surface form, so ordinary space-initial words and commas or semicolons deep in code should fire and prose fragments such as 'iment' in 'experiment' or 'aille' should be silent.

The pole is a shallow tokenizer-boundary effect that fires on every token with no leading space (including ordinary punctuation like ',', ';', ')'), so it should fire as hard on a comma or a full stop after a space-preceded word as on an identifier seam.

Χαλβάς
Με πλούσια σουσαμένια γεύση, o χαλβάς από ταχίνι διεκδικεί επάξια τον τίτλο του πιο υγιεινού γλυκού. Ελιές και τουρσιά

Μαλάκια, όπως τα καλαμαράκια και οι σουπιές γίνονται εκλεκτοί μεζέδες αλλά και εξαιρετικά κυρίως. Όπως και να τα φτιάξετε, στη σχάρα, βραστά, ψητά, μαγειρευτά τηγανητά ή γεμιστά με ποικιλία από μυρωδικά είναι απλά απολαυστικά.

readings.explanation: N53+ fires on a token that is a piece of a larger word-like composite rather than a word in its own right: subword/compound continuation fragments that attach to the preceding token with no space ('up' in signup, 'editor' in equationeditor, 'Value' in sameValue, 'net' in testnet, 'AA' in NEAA, 'cho' in ancho, 'ver' in Sil've'ru, a replacement char in a mojibake run) and the seam punctuation inside identifiers, tags and expressions ('->', '.', '_', '^', '>', '":'). Within one word activity jumps sharply at the non-initial piece (' sign' 1.1 vs 'up' 3.8; ' (NE' 1.9 vs 'AA' 3.8; ' same' 2.3 vs 'Value' 3.8), independent space-initial words are weak, and the firing rate rises with bracket/indent nesting (bracket depth 0: 49% vs 8+: 80%), so the feature is 'I am inside an unfinished composite unit', not any particular token or word.

The pole is an in-context copy/induction detector rather than a surface-composite detector: it peaks only where a chunk already emitted earlier in the same context (a repeated identifier, a repeated closing tag, a repeated list item) is being reproduced, so it should fall sharply when the earlier occurrence is removed even though the peaking piece is unchanged.

The pole is a code-structure/nesting feature that fires on any token sitting deep inside nested brackets or indentation, whatever its surface form, so ordinary space-initial words and commas or semicolons deep in code should fire and prose fragments such as 'iment' in 'experiment' or 'aille' should be silent.

The pole is a shallow tokenizer-boundary effect that fires on every token with no leading space (including ordinary punctuation like ',', ';', ')'), so it should fire as hard on a comma or a full stop after a space-preceded word as on an identifier seam.
